rows.name: SDL2 window surfaces
rows.reason: SDL2 window surfaces provide writable CPU pixels and presentation without implementing a graphics renderer. Respect format/pitch; reacquire surfaces after resize and avoid stale pixel pointers.

rows.name: CImg
rows.reason: Its C++ image container accepts pixel values and CImgDisplay opens a window and displays them; input parsing remains application code, and platform display dependencies remain.

rows.name: MiniFB (C library)
rows.reason: MiniFB directly supplies the small window-and-pixel-buffer API needed to present pixels parsed from stdin. Convert incoming pixels to its buffer format; native display-system dependencies remain.

rows.name: CImg
rows.reason: C++ display window shows application-managed pixels; program can parse stdin dimensions/pixels. Display requires X11 or GDI32, preventing complete display-server independence; original question makes this a caveat, not mandatory exclusion.

rows.name: Trados Studio (SDL Trados)
rows.reason: This translation-project editor provides translation memory and terminology tools, not a C/C++ library for creating windows or presenting pixel buffers; the SDL branding is unrelated.

rows.name: MiniFB
rows.reason: MiniFB creates windows from caller-owned 32-bit buffers. Backend display/channel layout must fit; Linux/Unix X11/Wayland backends do not establish display-server independence. Slow stdin must not stall events.

rows.name: SDL
rows.reason: SDL's verified SDL2 configuration supplies C/C++ windows, pixel surfaces and presentation; stdin parsing remains application code. Respect format/build backends; do not project live SDL3 features onto 2022.

rows.name: SFML 2.5
rows.reason: SFML 2.5 uploads RGBA arrays through textures/RenderWindow, adding sprite/texture objects. Graphics uses OpenGL; updates require correctly sized RGBA data. Display-server independence was not established.

rows.name: rawdraw / CNFG
rows.reason: rawdraw offers window creation, pixel-array blitting and presentation through a compact C interface. Backend configuration affects dependencies; current documentation says macOS support has moved to the attic.

rows.name: Trados Studio (SDL Trados)
rows.reason: Trados Studio manages translation projects, outside the requested C/C++ window/pixel-library role. Its SDL-associated name does not establish Simple DirectMedia Layer identity; undocumented capabilities remain unknown.

rows.name: Linux framebuffer device (fbdev)
rows.reason: Linux fbdev writes pixels without a desktop display server but does not create the requested window. Requires device access, compatible hardware and framebuffer-layout handling.

rows.name: SDL2
rows.reason: SDL2 window surfaces display pixels directly. Respect format/pitch; reacquire after resize; do not mix renderer/3D APIs. Backend support depends on build; dynamic loading does not eliminate display-system requirements.

rows.name: Fenster
rows.reason: Fenster wraps a window, RGB buffer and event/refresh loop in a small C header. Author article postdates question; Linux implementation still requires X11.

rows.name: CImg / CImgDisplay
rows.reason: CImgDisplay can open a window and display an image populated from stdin while handling window events. Larger image-processing scope than required; inspected implementation uses X11 or GDI32.

rows.name: SDL
rows.reason: The C library supports C++ and window/input handling; its SDL2 surface API directly presents application-generated pixels, with pixel-format conversion and an event loop required.
